title: Latent On-Policy Self-Distillation
hook: Every on-policy self-distillation method hand-picks what the teacher gets to see. LOPD makes that privileged context a learned vector instead of a design choice.
key_points: On-policy self-distillation gives a student dense supervision by letting a 'privileged' self-teacher see something extra — answers, feedback, skills, or reference trajectories.
Those privileged artifacts are hand-specified, which caps how far the loop can keep improving on its own.
LOPD retrieves relevant past experiences and compresses them into continuous latent tokens that condition the teacher, learned end-to-end.
The student generates trajectories from the task plus interaction history and gets token-level supervision at every visited prefix.
A privileged-margin objective keeps the learned latent context from collapsing or drifting during training.
Reported to beat RLVR, OPSD, SDPO and Skill-SD on agentic tool use and code generation, using under 30% of GRPO's rollout budget.
content_html: On-policy self-distillation is one of the cleaner recipes for letting an agent learn from its own experience: the model runs its own trajectories, and a "privileged" copy of itself — one that gets to see something the student doesn't — hands back dense, per-token supervision instead of a single sparse reward. The catch is that a human always decides what the privileged copy sees. Zhang et al. propose making that decision learnable.
extra_html:
Their method, LOPD, retrieves relevant past experiences and composes them into continuous latent tokens that condition the self-teacher. Nothing about the privileged signal is prescribed in advance — it's trained end-to-end alongside the policy, with a privileged-margin objective added to keep that learning stable. The student meanwhile generates trajectories from the task and its interaction history, and is supervised at every visited prefix.

The authors report gains over RLVR and over representative OPSD variants (OPSD, SDPO, Skill-SD) on both agentic tool use and code generation, and claim they pass GRPO and Skill-SD with under 30% of their rollout budget. Ablations are their main evidence that the learnable part is doing the work rather than the retrieval. August 2026, arXiv.

related.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation without Any Supervision
related.hook: Self-distillation that finally deserves the name: no ground truth, no bigger teacher — just a model voting against itself and fixing where it was confidently wrong.

related.title: Rethinking On-Policy Self-Distillation for Thinking Models
related.hook: Giving a model the answer as privileged context sounds like it should only help. For thinking models on long reasoning traces, it backfires — accuracy drops up to 17%, and this explains why.

related.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
related.hook: RL post-training gets pricier as models scale, since it needs the strong model's own rollouts. Direct-OPD reuses a cheap RL run on a small model instead, transferring the direction RL moved it.

related.title: Self-Supervised Visual On-Policy Distillation
related.hook: Distillation needs a teacher who knows more than the student. This paper gets that gap for free — not by informing the teacher, but by blinding the student.

flashcards.prompt: What is the 'privileged context' in on-policy self-distillation, and what does LOPD change about it?
flashcards.back_html: It's the extra information the self-teacher sees that the student doesn't — normally hand-specified (answers, feedback, skills, trajectories). LOPD replaces it with continuous latent tokens learned end-to-end from retrieved experience.

flashcards.prompt: Why do the authors argue hand-crafted privileged artifacts limit self-evolving agents?

choices.text: A designer has to prescribe the form of the privileged signal, so the loop can't keep learning what supervision it needs
They make the teacher larger than the student, which is too expensive to train
They force the student to train on off-policy data from other models

flashcards.explanation_html: LOPD's pitch is end-to-end learnability: if the privileged context is fixed by hand, scalability of continual self-improvement is capped by the designer's choice.

flashcards.prompt: Where does the student receive its training signal in LOPD?
flashcards.back_html: Dense token-level supervision from the privileged self-teacher at every visited prefix of the student's own trajectory — not just a single outcome reward at the end.

flashcards.prompt: What does LOPD's privileged-margin objective do?

choices.text: Stabilizes and regulates learning of the latent privileged context
Caps the number of experiences that can be retrieved per task
Penalizes the student for diverging from a frozen reference policy

flashcards.explanation_html: Once the privileged context is learned rather than given, it needs a constraint to stay useful — the margin objective is what keeps that learning well-behaved.
